group.passage:
Glaciers form when snow accumulates over time, turns to ice, and begins to flow outwards and downward under the pressure of the weight. Presently, glaciers occupy about 10 percent of the world’s total land area. Most of the world’s glaciers are found near the Poles, but glaciers exist on all of the world’s continents, even Africa. Australia doesn’t have any glaciers; however, it is considered part of Oceania, which includes several Pacific island chains and the large islands of Papua New Guinea and New Zealand. All of these islands have glaciers.
Glaciers require very specific climatic conditions. Most are found in regions of high snowfall in winter and cool temperature in summer. These conditions ensure the snow that accumulates in the winter doesn’t melt or evaporate. Such conditions typically prevail in polar and high alpine regions. Some glaciers are as small as football fields, while others grow to be over a hundred kilometers long. Two main types of glaciers are valley glaciers and continental glaciers known as ice sheets.
Glaciers can be thought as remnants from the last Ice Age, when ice covered nearly 32 percent of the land and 30 percent of the oceans. Within the past 750,000 years, scientists know that there have been eight Ice Age cycles, separated by warmer periods called interglacial periods. Currently, the Earth is nearing the end of an interglacial, meaning that another Ice Age is due in a few thousand years though greenhouse effect may delay the onset.
Today, glaciers are not only tourist attractions but also a natural resource, and people all over the world are trying to harness the power of these frozen streams. In Switzerland’s Rhone Valley, for example, farmers have irrigated their crops for hundreds of years by channeling meltwater from glaciers to their fields. Scientists and engineers in Norway, Canada, New Zealand and the Alps have also worked together to tap into glacial resources, using electricity that has been generated in part by damming glacial meltwater.

questions.stem: According to the passage, which of the following statements is correct?

options.A: People can appreciate glaciers in Australia and New Zealand.
options.B: The Earth is at present in the end of the last Ice Age.
options.C: Glaciers always take up lots of living space and do nothing good to humans.
options.D: Glaciers, usually found near the Poles, come in different size.

questions.stem: Which is NOT the condition for the formation of glaciers according to the article?

options.A: A place where the temperature is quite low in summer.
options.B: A region of sufficient snow and abundant rainfall.
options.C: An area where snow piles up for a long period of time.
options.D: A location where the accumulation of snow does not easily melt.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about Ice Ages is NOT true?

options.A: The rainy periods between Ice Ages are called interglacial periods.
options.B: Global warming is said to postpone the beginning of another Ice Age.
options.C: In the last Ice Age, about one-third of the ocean is covered with ice.
options.D: Eight Ice Age cycles have been identified in history.

questions.stem: What is the main idea of the last paragraph of the passage?

options.A: The threats glaciers pose to human beings.
options.B: The influences glaciers have on humans.
options.D: The places people can find glaciers.
